newsitem.title: KENYA: Rwanda denies asking Libya to mediate on Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda denies asking Libya to mediate on Zaire.

text.p: Rwanda denied on Thursday asking Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi to mediate in the conflict in eastern Zaire.
"The government of Rwanda has never sought Libyan assistance to resolve the crisis in Zaire," said Joseph Bideri, spokesman for Rwandan President Pasteur Bizimungu.

"The president has full confidence in the ongoing regional initiative...and there is absolutely no need to look for alternative leadership in this regard," Bideri said by telephone from the Rwandan capital Kigali.

Earlier this week Libyan news agency JANA reported Gaddafi was contacting leaders of countries involved in the Great Lakes region conflict to arrange a meeting after receiving a request to help mediate from Bizimungu.

Zairean rebels with links to Rwanda seized control of a swathe of territory in eastern Zaire last October and November, ousting the government army and displacing hundreds of thousands of Rwandan Hutu refugees.
Last week, Gaddafi expressed support for Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko, arguing only he could guarantee the unity of the vast and ethnically-diverse state.
